questions: If n is zero, should the function return an empty Counter or raise an error?
If n is negative, should the function raise an error, return an empty Counter, or something else?
Should the seed be applied globally (affecting other random calls) or locally (only for this function)?
If seed is provided, should the random.seed be reset after generation to avoid affecting subsequent randomness?
Is the list of letters required to be stored as a list, or can an alternative data structure be used as long as the Counter is correct?
Should the function handle non-integer n (e.g., float) by converting or raising an error?
If n is very large, is there any performance or memory constraint (e.g., must use list, not generator)?
Should the Counter be returned in any specific order (e.g., sorted) or is any order acceptable?
